Title: Diagnosis  
Details: 

The bug report describes an issue with `PosixParser` when the flag `stopAtNonOption` is enabled. The problem is that after encountering a non-recognized long option (like `--zop`), the parser continues to process tokens by "bursting" or splitting them around `=` and interpreting them as individual options or arguments, instead of keeping the entire remaining tokens as literal arguments (not splitting or processing).

Looking at the test case, it passes `--zop==1` which is an unrecognized long option followed by `-abtoast` and `--b=bar`.

Inspecting the relevant methods:
1. The method `burstToken(String token, boolean stopAtNonOption)` shows how tokens starting with a single dash are split into individual options, unless `stopAtNonOption` is true and an unknown option is found, in which case it calls `process(token.substring(i))` to stop bursting.

2. The method `process(String value)` is responsible for handling "leftover" tokens. The important part is that when no current option is being processed, it sets `eatTheRest = true;` adds `--` and then adds the remaining token as is.

The critical missing piece seems to be how `PosixParser` treats unrecognized long options when the `stopAtNonOption` flag is enabled. Instead of treating the unrecognized long option as a stop indicator and leaving the rest of the command line unprocessed (kept as raw arguments), the parser improperly "bursts" or further processes tokens like `-abtoast` by splitting them as individual options `-a`, `-b`, and the attached argument `toast`. This is inconsistent with the behavior expected when a `--` or unknown long option is encountered.

Hence the root cause is:  
The `PosixParser` does not correctly respect the `stopAtNonOption` flag after encountering an unrecognized long option and continues processing (bursting) next tokens rather than preserving them as raw arguments.

This behavior causes the number of extra arguments to differ from expectation, leading to the failure in the test `testStop3`.

Next, it is likely the bug lies in the core parsing method in `PosixParser` that handles recognized and unrecognized long options and decides when to stop processing tokens and when to "burst" tokens into individual options.

To confirm exactly which method is responsible for handling long options and deciding whether to stop or continue parsing, locating the main parsing loop or long option handling method in `PosixParser` would be helpful.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
